evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database)
evidence.field: 形義通解; oracle-bone and bronze uses; Shuowen; Guangyun
evidence.text: The entry interprets 干 in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions as a shield, sometimes decorated with feathers, and links its defensive use with later senses of protecting or guarding. It cites oracle-bone example 合集 28059, “弜令戍干衛,” bronze 豦簋 “干戈,” and the *Book of Documents* 牧誓 passage “稱爾戈，比爾干，立爾矛.” It also records Shuowen’s Han-period analysis 犯也。从反入，从一 as a separate historical explanation. The entry reports Xu Zhongshu’s alternative that certain oracle-bone 干 forms are variants of 單 and depict a forked hunting implement. Its Guangyun entry gives 古寒切 and the Middle Chinese category 見母, level tone, 寒 rhyme, open division, first grade.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 干

evidence.source: CASE Press / National Taiwan University science communication
evidence.text: The article describes proposed Shang forms for 干 but treats their identification as debated. It gives the mid-Western Zhou 豦簋 inscription as the secure attestation and describes the sign as shield-like with a forked top. Later Western Zhou forms regularize the upper feature into a short horizontal stroke, retained in later script traditions. This supports graphic change as reported by the article, but its descriptions do not establish a single uncontested reading for every proposed Shang form.
evidence.title: 商周時期的防護裝具與兵器：甲、冑、干、盾（四）

evidence.source: 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心
evidence.text: Su Jianzhou reviews competing readings of Western Zhou bronze signs and argues from inscriptional contexts, including 豦簋, that the forms under discussion represent 干. The article documents scholarly disagreement over the identification of particular bronze shapes and their distinction from 盾; it supports the shield reading as a substantial scholarly analysis, not an uncontested reading of every early form.
evidence.title: 蘇建洲：西周金文“干”字再議

evidence.field: 乾 formation, readings, and textual citations
evidence.text: The dictionary quotes Shuowen’s analysis of 乾 as 上出也, 从乙, with 倝 as the phonetic element, and records the fanqie readings 渠焉切 and 古寒切. It distinguishes qián for emergence upward, heaven, and the trigrams/hexagrams from gān for dry. For gān it cites the *Book of Odes*, 王風·中谷有蓷, “中谷有蓷，暵其乾矣,” and later parched/dried senses in the *Zuo zhuan* and *Shan Hai Jing*. These citations attest the dry sense in the received classical text tradition but do not date the beginning of that word or establish a semantic bridge to 干 “shield.”
evidence.title: A00044 乾 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database)
evidence.text: The page gives Shuowen’s 乾 analysis 从乙 with 倝聲 and two Guangyun readings: 古寒切, classified as 見母 level tone, 寒 rhyme, open division, first grade; and 渠焉切, 群母 level tone, 仙 rhyme, open division, third grade. This independently supports the historical dictionary’s distinct traditional readings for the dry and qián/heaven words and reports 倝 as the phonetic element in the Shuowen analysis. It does not independently establish 倝’s original depicted referent.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 乾

evidence.text: The dictionary says 幹 is not recorded as an entry in Shuowen and describes it as a vulgar form of 榦, with construction from 倝 as phonetic. It records the meanings of a principal beam or stem, a person or thing’s main body, main/primary, ability, matter, and to manage or engage in. Its cited examples include Han and later literary sources. This account does not show that 干 “shield” is a phonetic or semantic component of 幹.
evidence.title: A01196 幹 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database)
evidence.field: 幹 senses and cited textual examples
evidence.text: The entry records 幹 for an implement’s main shaft in the *Liji*, a body’s frame or bones in the *Zuo zhuan*, and a figurative basis or mainstay in the *Yi*. It also lists later senses including ability, management, and business or affairs. Its Guangyun reading is 古案切, classified as 見母, level/去 tone category, 寒 rhyme, open division, first grade. The entry links 幹 and 干 as spellings in its dictionary treatment, but does not demonstrate an ancient derivation from the shield graph.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 幹

evidence.field: file description, source attribution, and license
evidence.text: The exact lead file 干-seal.svg is described as a Shuowen seal-style depiction of 干 and identifies its image source as s01611 on hanziyuan.net. Its page links sources including Sinica, Chinese Etymology, the CUHK character database, and Chinese Text Project. The page’s licensing section states public domain and says attribution is appreciated but not required; it also displays a permission note referring to Richard Sears’s agreement. The file is a modern vector representation of a seal-script form, not an artifact image or evidence for the shield interpretation. The alternative exact lead Shuowen Seal Radical 047.svg was searched/opened but its description page could not be retrieved by the web tool.
evidence.title: File:干-seal.svg

This general official page was accessible, but the character-specific official records for 干, 乾, and 幹 could not be opened in this session.

Local rows are identified as supplied local data, not external page evidence.

evidence.source: Local primary reading data supplied in input
evidence.text: The supplied Baxter–Sagart 2014 rows give 干 MC kan, OC *kˤa[r] for shield (with additional homographic gloss rows pole, piece/item, placename); 乾 MC kan, OC *[k]ˤar for dry and MC gjen, OC *[g](r)ar for heaven/heavenly; 幹 MC kanH, OC *[k]ˤar-s for stem/framework. These are readings from the named reconstruction system and preserve its distinct rows and notation. They do not establish a graphic or phonetic relationship between 干 and either 乾 or 幹.

search_audit.outcome: Opened and inspected the CUHK entries for 干, 乾, and 幹; Taiwan Ministry dictionary entries for 乾 and 幹; paleographic research pages at NTU CASE and Fudan; Commons description page for the exact 干-seal.svg lead; and Unicode Unihan documentation. The individual Unihan records for all three characters were attempted and inaccessible. The Commons page for the exact alternate seal-radical lead and the direct SVG were attempted but inaccessible; no pixels were independently inspected through the web tool.

gaps: No independently verified character-specific Unicode Unihan page could be opened for 干, 乾, or 幹. The exact supplied local kMandarin rows were checked and are reported as local data only; official click-through verification remains unavailable.
The supplied Baxter–Sagart rows were checked exactly, but no upstream B–S character page was inspected; no external citation is claimed for those local values.

The CUHK entry reports defensive use in oracle-bone and bronze contexts, while the NTU article identifies mid-Western Zhou 豦簋 as the secure graph attestation and treats proposed Shang identifications as disputed. The exact earliest inscription date and a fully established chronology of shield versus defend senses remain unresolved.

The source-word chronology and semantic link between 干 ‘shield’ and the separate word written 乾 ‘dry’ are not established. The *Book of Odes* citation attests the dry sense in that transmitted text, not when it originated. No ancient object-name/pronunciation is recovered; no shield-name phonetic borrowing is needed for the shield-pictograph account.

The relationship between 干 ‘shield’ and 幹 ‘stem/framework’ is not established as an ancient graphic derivation. Ministry dictionary describes 幹 as a vulgar form of 榦 and assigns 倝 a phonetic role; it does not identify 干 as a phonetic component.
The old phonetic value or depicted referent of 倝 was not independently researched here. No claim is made that its modern or reconstructed sound alone proves the phonetic history.

Commons’ exact file page supports the identity and public-domain licensing claim for the seal-style vector, but the image itself was not visually inspected. It is a modern seal-script rendering and does not document dated artifact forms; no historical glyph image is selected.
The alternative exact Commons file Shuowen Seal Radical 047.svg returned a cache-miss/access failure. No file identity, pixels, or rights claim is made for that lead.
